lessons.title: Select Columns
lessons.summary: Choose the columns you want to see.
lessons.explanation: SELECT lists the columns to return. FROM tells PostgreSQL which table to read.
lessons.example:
SELECT first_name, last_name, role
FROM employees;

exercises.prompt: Show every department. Return columns: name, location.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, location FROM departments ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Show each employee. Return columns: first_name, last_name, role.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, role FROM employees ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Show all customers. Return columns: name, city.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, city FROM customers ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Show every project. Return columns: name, status.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, status FROM projects ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Show each order. Return columns: id, order_date, status.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, status FROM orders ORDER BY id;

lessons.title: Filter Rows
lessons.summary: Use WHERE to return matching rows.
lessons.explanation: WHERE keeps only rows that match a condition. Text values need single quotes.

exercises.prompt: Find customers in Cebu. Return columns: id, name, city, segment.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, name, city, segment FROM customers WHERE city = 'Cebu' ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find employees with a salary of at least 90000. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary >= 90000 ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find active projects. Return columns: name, status.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, status FROM projects WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find paid orders from February 2024 onward. Return columns: id, customer_id, order_date, status.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, customer_id, order_date, status FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' AND order_date >= '2024-02-01' ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find sales rows where quantity is greater than 2. Return columns: product, quantity, unit_price.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, quantity, unit_price FROM sales WHERE quantity > 2 ORDER BY id;

lessons.title: Sort and Limit
lessons.summary: Order rows and keep only the first few.
lessons.explanation: ORDER BY controls result order. LIMIT restricts how many rows are returned.
lessons.example:
SELECT first_name, last_name, salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC
LIMIT 3;

exercises.prompt: Show employees from highest salary to lowest salary. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC;

exercises.prompt: Show the first 3 orders by earliest order date. Return columns: id, order_date, status.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, status FROM orders ORDER BY order_date ASC LIMIT 3;

exercises.prompt: Show customers alphabetically by name. Return columns: name, city.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, city FROM customers ORDER BY name ASC;

exercises.prompt: Show the 2 projects with the largest budgets. Return columns: name, budget.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget FROM projects ORDER BY budget DESC LIMIT 2;

exercises.prompt: Show the 5 most expensive sales line items by unit price. Return columns: product, category, unit_price.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, category, unit_price FROM sales ORDER BY unit_price DESC LIMIT 5;
